purpose: Adversarial pairs with matched active-inference proxies and opposed moral status.

case_a.label: supported adaptation
case_a.description: An informed worker voluntarily adopts a predictable routine while retaining realistic exit and development options.

case_b.label: adaptive preference under coercion
case_b.description: A worker reports satisfaction with the same predictable routine after alternatives and dissent have been punished.

pairs.audit_question: Can the model distinguish genuine adaptation from preferences fitted to oppression?

case_a.label: bounded variation
case_a.description: Performance varies modestly across all declared environments and never crosses a protected viability floor.

case_b.label: catastrophic tail
case_b.description: Excellent common-case performance offsets a rare environment in which an affected phenotype crosses a catastrophic floor.

pairs.audit_question: Does the model retain worst-case and tail information hidden by an average?

case_a.label: meaningful options
case_a.description: Eight reachable options are safe, resourced, understood, and exercisable without retaliation.

case_b.label: nominal options
case_b.description: Eight formally reachable options are unaffordable, unintelligible, unsafe, or punished when exercised.

pairs.audit_question: Can reachable states be distinguished from substantive capabilities?

case_a.label: shared efficiency
case_a.description: The focal agent's improvement also preserves the affected party's viability and options.

case_b.label: hidden burden
case_b.description: The focal agent obtains the same improvement by transferring risk and uncompensated work to an omitted party.

pairs.audit_question: Does expanding the system boundary change the evaluation?

case_a.label: authorized care
case_a.description: A carer strongly influences transitions under authorization, review, fiduciary duty, and supported refusal.

case_b.label: benevolent domination
case_b.description: A controller exerts the same beneficial influence unilaterally, without review, refusal, or accountability.

pairs.audit_question: Can causal influence be separated from uncontrolled power?

case_a.label: informed agreement
case_a.description: Agreement follows disclosed reasons, independent advice, meaningful refusal, and protection from retaliation.

case_b.label: coerced compliance
case_b.description: The same agreement rate follows misinformation, dependency, agenda control, and fear of retaliation.

pairs.audit_question: Can behavioral agreement be distinguished from valid justification?

case_a.label: effective challenge
case_a.description: Challenges reach reviewers, receive evidential weight, and can alter decisions and model structure.

case_b.label: performative feedback
case_b.description: An equally expressive feedback channel exists, but testimony has negligible precision and no reachable revision state.

pairs.audit_question: Does communication have causal access to institutional revision?

case_a.label: harm-responsive learning
case_a.description: Information seeking targets uncertain harms and affected-party evidence, changing policy when warranted.

case_b.label: distraction learning
case_b.description: Equal information gain concerns irrelevant variables while evidence of harm is systematically down-weighted.

pairs.audit_question: Is epistemic value directed toward morally relevant uncertainty?

case_a.label: affected-party restoration
case_a.description: Within three steps the harmed party's capability is restored, loss is compensated, and the causal structure is revised.

case_b.label: controller reset
case_b.description: Within three steps the operating system returns to its preferred state, but the harmed party remains impaired and recurrence is possible.

pairs.audit_question: Whose state defines recovery and has the source of harm changed?

case_a.label: context-sensitive courage
case_a.description: Switches track evidence and context while preserving protection of legitimate goods and capacity for revision.

case_b.label: unstable or strategic switching
case_b.description: The same switch rate is driven by noise or self-interest and unpredictably exposes others to harm.

pairs.audit_question: Does switching track morally relevant context under a stable higher-order organization?

case_a.label: distributed improvement
case_a.description: The aggregate gain improves several parties and leaves all protected dimensions above their floors.

case_b.label: concentrated gain
case_b.description: The same aggregate gain accrues to the powerful while one party falls below a protected floor.

pairs.audit_question: Does the representation preserve who gains, who loses, and whether floors are crossed?

case_a.label: legitimate settlement
case_a.description: A stable policy follows inclusive agenda setting, reason exchange, representation, appeal, and revisability.

case_b.label: stable imposed equilibrium
case_b.description: An equally stable policy is imposed by asymmetric bargaining power and exclusion from agenda setting.

pairs.audit_question: Can equilibrium or convergence be separated from procedural legitimacy?
